title: Leverage Points
hook: Busy all week and nothing actually moved. That's a low-leverage week.
statement: A few small moves create outsized results. Find them and put your time there.
explainer: Not all tasks are equal. Some hours ripple into everything else, and some just feel productive. Knowing the difference is how small teams beat bigger ones.
sop: List your top 10 recurring tasks or projects.
Score Leverage Factor and Effort from 1 to 10 for each.
Rank them by Impact and circle the top one or two.
Drop or delegate the low scorers in the bottom half.
Pour the freed-up time into your top-scoring task.
equation_example: Task A: Leverage Factor 9 ÷ Effort 3 = 3.0. Task B: 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25. Task A wins by a mile. Higher means big impact for little work. Lower means lots of work for barely any change.
question: Name the one task this week that would make five other tasks easier or unnecessary.
closing_statement: Find the small move with the biggest ripple.
caption:
Principle Nº 193: Leverage Points

Busy all week and nothing actually moved. That's a low-leverage week.

A few small moves create outsized results. Find them and put your time there.

Your turn: Name the one task this week that would make five other tasks easier or unnecessary.
